誰來決定哪些記憶被放進影片: Who decides which memories go into the film
一群長輩在社區據點學拍片，把搬遷前的街區留在手機裡。: A group of elders learn to shoot video at a community hub, keeping the pre-demolition streets in their phones.
街屋一戶一戶搬走之後，據點的社工發現，長輩聊起舊事時總是說得很熱鬧，可是講完就散: After the shophouses emptied one household at a time, the hub's social worker noticed that elders spoke vividly about the old days, but once they finished the talk scattered and nothing was kept. The video group borrowed a small classroom at the hub, meeting on Wednesday afternoons; the first class had one requirement: bring an old photograph.
阿霞帶來一張碼頭邊的合照。照片裡的雜貨店早就拆了，她叫不出店名，卻記得每個人站的: A-hsia brought a group photo taken by the wharf. The grocery store in it was long demolished; she could not name it but remembered where everyone stood. The group scanned the photo and projected it on the wall, asking her to go person by person. At the third person she paused, and said this one later moved away and was never in touch again.
課程後半段，每位學員用手機拍一段短片，剪接由自己決定，小組只示範軟體怎麼用。六支: In the second half of the course each learner shot a short video on a phone, deciding the editing themselves while the group only demonstrated the software. On the day the six films screened at the hub, one person walked out halfway, saying he needed a moment. When he came back, he asked if it could be played once more.
照片是最不需要解釋的東西。長輩不用先學會『創作』這個詞，只要說這是誰、站在哪裡，: A photo is the thing that needs the least explanation. Elders don't have to learn the word 'creation' first; they just say who this is and where they stood, and the story comes out on its own.
剪接的時候意見不同怎麼辦？: What do you do when you disagree over the editing?
有一支片子，我覺得某段太長，建議剪掉。作者說不要，那段是他太太的聲音。我就閉嘴了: On one film I thought a passage ran too long and suggested cutting it. The maker refused — that part was his wife's voice. I shut up. At the screening, that passage was the quietest moment in the room.
一開始為什麼願意來？: Why were you willing to come at first?
社工說有地方可以聊天，我就來了。聽說要學拍片，我以為很難，結果第一天只是看照片。: The social worker said there was a place to chat, so I came. When I heard we'd learn to shoot video I thought it would be hard, but the first day was just looking at photos.
看到自己的片子在牆上放，是什麼感覺？: How did it feel to see your own film on the wall?
很怪。我平常不會看自己，那天看了好幾次。有人說拍得好，我說不是我拍得好，是那個地: Strange. I don't usually look at myself, but that day I watched several times. Someone said it was well shot; I said it wasn't me shooting well, that place was just good to begin with.
我怕片子放到網路上，鄰居會知道補償的事。所以我只同意在據點放。他們有再問我一次，: I was afraid that if the film went online, neighbours would learn about the compensation. So I only agreed to show it at the hub. They asked me once more, and then I felt safe.
週日，他們把一週的話說給觀眾聽: On Sunday, they tell the audience a week's worth of words
週日休假的移工與劇場工作者，把工作與生活經驗編成短劇。: Migrant workers off on Sunday and theatre workers turn their work and life experiences into short plays.
每個週日下午，車站旁的一間排練室會坐滿人。有人剛下夜班，有人從很遠的縣市搭車過來: Every Sunday afternoon a rehearsal room by the station fills up. Some have just come off a night shift, some have travelled from far-off counties. They take off their coats, form a circle, play games for twenty minutes, then start telling what happened this week.
劇團的導演不寫劇本。她請大家把想講的事寫成三句話，再從裡面挑一句，變成一場戲。有: The company's director writes no script. She asks everyone to put what they want to say into three sentences, then pick one and turn it into a scene. One scene had a single action: a person opening and closing an umbrella over and over, while the others took turns asking him, 'Still waiting?'
演出在廣場邊的空地。台下有路過的人，有朋友，也有雇主派來的司機。最後一場謝幕時，: The performance was on open ground beside the plaza. In the audience were passers-by, friends, and a driver sent by an employer. At the final curtain no one bowed; they just stood, looking at the audience, until someone began to clap.
你怎麼決定演什麼？: How do you decide what to perform?
我不決定。我只負責問問題，例如『這句話如果是一個動作，會是什麼』。答案都在他們身: I don't. I only ask questions, like 'if this sentence were an action, what would it be?' The answers are all in them.
有沒有遇過不想公開的事？: Has anyone had something they didn't want made public?
有。有些事他們說完就想收回去。我們的規則是，說在排練室裡的話，沒有人同意就不會演: Yes. Some things they want to take back after saying them. Our rule is that what's said in the rehearsal room is never performed without consent.
週日是我唯一可以說話說很久的日子。平常說的都是工作上的句子。: Sunday is the only day I can talk at length. The rest of the week I only speak work sentences.
演出之後有什麼改變？: Did anything change after the performance?
有一個路人跟我說，他以前以為我們都不太說話。我說我們很會說，只是你沒有聽到。: A passer-by told me he used to think we didn't talk much. I said we talk plenty — you just hadn't heard it.
一條被加蓋的舊水圳，成了孩子與居民一起行走的路線。: An old covered-over irrigation channel becomes a route children and residents walk together.
水圳在六十年前被蓋住了，現在上面是停車格和騎樓。要找到它，得看地圖，也得看房子的: The channel was covered over sixty years ago; above it now are parking spaces and arcades. To find it you have to read a map, and also read the way the houses face. The older generation say that when it rains, the ground at certain corners goes wet first.
行走團第一次帶小學生走這條路線，沒有講解，只發一張空白地圖。孩子們沿路用腳步、粉: The first time the walking group led primary-school pupils along the route, there was no explanation — just a blank map each. Along the way the children marked, with footsteps, chalk and sound, where they thought the water should pass. Halfway, one child crouched, put an ear to the ground, and said they could hear it.
後來學校把這些地圖貼在走廊上，居民路過時會停下來看。有位阿公指著其中一張，說他小: Later the school put these maps up along the corridor, and residents passing by would stop to look. One grandfather pointed at one of them and said he had caught fish here as a child — only this time he finally knew the children's drawn turn was right.
為什麼不先告訴孩子水圳在哪裡？: Why not tell the children where the channel is first?
答案先給了，他們就只是在確認。我們想要的是他們自己找，找錯也沒關係。: Give the answer first and they're only confirming it. We want them to find it themselves — getting it wrong is fine too.
馬路。很多路段要穿越車流，我們得拜託家長志工一起顧。這比藝術本身還花時間。: The roads. Many stretches cross traffic, so we had to ask parent volunteers to help watch. That took more time than the art itself.
他們開始注意地上的東西，排水孔、地磚的縫。回家還會問爸媽『這裡以前是不是有水』。: They started noticing things on the ground — drains, the gaps between tiles. At home they'd even ask their parents, 'was there water here before?'
看到孩子畫的地圖，你想到什麼？: What did the children's maps make you think of?
想到以前。我說不出來，就指給他們看。他們聽得很認真，我就講了很久。: The old days. I couldn't put it into words, so I pointed it out to them. They listened so earnestly that I talked for a long time.
把一輩子的路線縫成一塊布: Stitching a lifetime's routes into one cloth
長者用針線記下年輕時的工作與搬家路線，拼成共同的布地圖。: Elders record the work and moving routes of their youth in needle and thread, piecing together a shared cloth map.
據點的角落有一張大長桌，桌上永遠有幾團線。每週二上午，十來位阿嬤會到這裡，不是來: In a corner of the hub is a big long table, always with a few balls of thread on it. Every Tuesday morning a dozen or so grandmothers come — not to learn embroidery, but to 'mend things'. The teacher says mending is what they know best, so it starts from mending.
有一天，老師請大家用線畫出自己年輕時走過的路。有人從工廠走到宿舍，有人從娘家走到: One day the teacher asked everyone to draw, in thread, the routes they walked in their youth. One went from the factory to the dormitory, one from her parents' home to her husband's, one spent a lifetime going back and forth among three streets. When a stitch went crooked, everyone laughed and said the road was never straight to begin with.
六十幾塊小布被縫在一起，成了一張大地圖。展出那天，一位阿嬤站在自己那一塊前面，沒: Sixty-odd small cloths were sewn together into one big map. On opening day a grandmother stood before her own piece, saying nothing. Asked what she was looking at, she said: I'm looking at the road I walked — so small, it turns out, and so long.
她們不覺得自己會創作，但補東西做了五十年。我只是請她們把同樣的手，用在另一件事上: They don't think they can create, but they've mended things for fifty years. I just asked them to use the same hands on something else.
有沒有遇到不想講的事？: Was there anything they didn't want to talk about?
有。有人縫到一半，線就停了。我們不問，等她自己想繼續。: Yes. Someone stopped mid-stitch and the thread just stopped. We don't ask; we wait until she wants to continue.
你縫的是哪一段路？: Which stretch of road did you stitch?
從工廠走回宿舍的那條。每天天黑才走，很怕。我縫得很細，因為走了很多次。: The one from the factory back to the dormitory. I walked it only after dark, very scared. I stitched it finely, because I walked it so many times.
看到自己的布被掛起來，你覺得呢？: How did you feel seeing your cloth hung up?
我以前做的東西都是別人在用，這次是第一次，是給別人看的。: What I made before was always for others to use; this is the first time it's for others to look at.
